item.title: Understanding Tensions in Digital Supply Chain Ecosystems
item.content:encoded:
Robert Glenn Richey, Jr., Auburn University

Tarun Agrawal, Chalmers University of Technology

Jag Srai, University of Cambridge

Medo Pournader, University of Melbourne

Organizations in digital supply chain ecosystems navigate competing demands: they must increase data sharing and coordination while protecting sensitive information and maintaining control. Digital transformation has fundamentally altered supply chains from linear, firm-centered structures to complex ecosystems with shared platforms, distributed decision-making, and multiple interdependent actors. This creates new challenges because responsiveness—the ability to adapt behaviors and strategies to changing conditions—now requires coordination across organizational boundaries, with participants having unequal information access and conflicting incentives.

This special issue explores how digital ecosystems reshape supply chain responsiveness, focusing on converting digital visibility into coordinated adjustment without creating vulnerability. It welcomes conceptual, quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-method studies that extend the responsiveness framework by examining how digital infrastructures, artificial intelligence, blockchain, and data governance enable or constrain ecosystem-level adaptation while addressing cybersecurity, sustainability, and accountability concerns.

Appel publié par International Journal of Physical Distribution & Logistics Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • AI-enabled supply chain ecosystems and algorithmic decision-making
  • Data ownership, access rights, and information asymmetry
  • Digital infrastructures and supply chain responsiveness
  • Digital product passports and traceability systems
  • Digital supply chain ecosystems and platform governance
  • Digitalization in circular supply chains
  • Governance mechanisms for ecosystem responsiveness
  • Institutional and regulatory drivers of transparency
  • Risk propagation in interconnected supply chains
  • Agility, flexibility, adaptability, and resilience
  • Openness, protection, speed, and strategic flexibility trade-offs
